purpose: Preflight evidence for the eight swiss_schools_* sources: what each board actually publishes TODAY, before any adapter is written.

measured_live_state.reading: Six of the seven boards reachable by a single URL publish ZERO offers right now, and that is the NORMAL state of a watchlist: a school posts a vacancy every few months. Only haut-lac (1) and ISCS (2) have anything today.

why_this_changes_the_adapter_design: Every adapter written so far RAISES when a sweep finds nothing, because for a job board an empty sweep means a broken parser. For the schools that rule is inverted: an empty board is the expected state, and raising would make six of eight sources fail every day. What must be preserved instead is the legacy's 'verified empty': the page was fetched, its structure was RECOGNISED, and only then is zero reported as healthy. Core therefore needs a per-school structural marker — present and no offers is a complete, empty sweep; absent is a visible failure.
complications_to_plan_for: inspired and nae are NOT one board each: they sweep several schools per source, each with its own careers URL and a facet filter on the school name (SuccessFactors and Nord Anglia portals). A block on one must not be reported N times — the legacy stops the run on the first block for exactly that reason.
isp does not use the shared base: 467 lines with its own normalize (Workday), and it builds its listing URL dynamically.
ecolint declares five pages; the capture shows page 1 and page 2 are byte-identical, so its pagination needs the same treatment myScience got.

The schools are WATCHLIST_SOURCE: the legacy exempts them from the no-news backoff on purpose, because the rare event is the valuable one. Core has no equivalent backoff, so nothing to port, but the cadence decision belongs with the owner.
